specName: The Hierarchical Requirement Designer in the Standalone Host
last_action: living specs evaluated — no capabilities matched

FR-001.title: Offer the designer type as Hierarchical Requirement Designer

FR-002.title: Recognise a requirement document by its envelope alone, ahead of the other .md owners

FR-003.title: Add an existing requirement document as a designer document without changing it

FR-004.title: Keep the document when its registration is deleted; create the registration with the first setting

FR-005.title: Create a new document from the binding template byte for byte

FR-006.title: One page that scrolls top to bottom, no tree beside it

FR-007.title: Items as boxes with requirements then sub-items to their right

FR-008.title: Levels that fit, a mark for those that do not, focus with a trail, not stored

FR-009.title: Number beside the title, tags below it, description under it

FR-010.title: Collapse control left of every title, kept when reopened

FR-011.title: The Knowledge designer looks in both themes, outside a table too

FR-012.title: Add without a dialog by a control and by a named key

FR-013.title: Drag an item with its content, or a requirement

FR-014.title: Confirm before deleting an entry that holds anything or is named

FR-015.title: Assessment icon at the top right, rolling up in a collapsed item

FR-016.title: The icon opens the list of its assessments to add, change, remove, resolve

FR-017.title: Typing # opens the lookup of entries of the same document

FR-018.title: Selecting a reference box shows its target without writing the file

FR-019.title: Narrow by tag, category, state and an item pattern with * and ?

FR-020.title: Sort requirements within each item without changing the file

FR-021.title: A finding stays listed under a filter and shows its entry

FR-022.title: Read an outside change again and keep what was collapsed

FR-023.title: Tell the person and offer reload or keep when unsaved edits meet an outside change

FR-024.title: Refuse an edit against a changed file, never merge

FR-025.title: Tell the person when an outside change ended the undo history

FR-026.title: Make the model change and the fixture bytes of every gesture

FR-027.title: Report each finding at its place; an unreadable file read-only, never written

FR-028.title: Read and write declared registration blocks; keep an undeclared one

FR-029.title: FBL host conformance with bullets, passing every fixture

FR-030.title: DESL host conformance with the hierarchy surface kind

FR-031.title: DED host conformance: envelope, version, never changed

FR-032.title: The hierarchy surface is shared host work, not module code

decisions.decision: The standalone host build of the Hierarchical Requirement Designer is specified here as spec 029, not in standalone .spec-workflow/
decisions.why: The maintainer asked on 2026-10-14 when T070 of spec 028 came up, as for spec 025

decisions.decision: Each user story passes spec 028 scenarios of the same story by reference and adds only what this host decides
decisions.why: Copying them would let the two specifications drift

decisions.decision: Plan now against the host spec 025 leaves; the first task reads the host again and corrects paths
decisions.why: The spec asks for a re-read when building starts; the decisions do not depend on where a type lives
decisions.rejected: Waiting with the plan until spec 025 is done

decisions.decision: Eleven standalone pull requests: two FBL, routing, model, surface, then one per user story
decisions.why: Host order is model, persistence, wire, client UI; each later story ships alone
decisions.rejected: One pull request per layer across all stories

decisions.decision: The envelope claims a .md through the FBL library marker routing, asked first in ToolRouter
decisions.why: Agent Behavior Modelling is a diagram and routes first today; FBL 12 defines marker claims and the library has them
decisions.rejected: A content check in the designer router alone

decisions.decision: A designer document may have no registration; it is created with the first setting outside the history; deleting it keeps the body
decisions.why: FR-002, FR-004 and the binding createOnFirstPlacement
decisions.rejected: Creating an empty registration on open

decisions.decision: Adding an existing .md: accepted with the envelope, refused without it, never written
decisions.why: Routing by envelope already makes it a designer document; the refusal names the line to write
decisions.rejected: A consent dialog that writes the envelope

decisions.decision: A second session contract IHierarchySurfaceSession beside ITableDesignerSession, and the whole model sent on every change
decisions.why: The table members cannot serve a page; 500 requirements fit in SC-003
decisions.rejected: Deltas as the table sends them

decisions.decision: Unsaved edits are the field being typed; Keep my text re-plans one value against the new file
decisions.why: Designers write behind; replacing one value is an edit, not a merge

decisions.decision: Ctrl+Enter and Ctrl+Shift+Enter as context-action shortcuts are the host help; mdi-comment-multiple-outline for several
decisions.why: The host has no help screen; shortcuts show in ribbon and menus

decisions.decision: Amend spec 029 where the definition disagrees: title is the base name, SC-009 exempts std.missingId, 23 fixtures, outside-history writes
decisions.why: The definition wins, as the spec says
decisions.rejected: Leaving the spec at odds with the fixtures

expectations: Changes to a specification language or the definition
Agent Behavior Modelling on the bullets family
A host library that interprets .des files
Merging the edits of two writers

intent: Build the Hierarchical Requirement Designer in the standalone host from the definition spec 028 merged

plan.summary: Plan, research, data model, three contracts and quickstart for building the designer in the standalone host in eleven pull requests
plan.key_finding: The host assumes a designer document always has a registration and routes by registration only; envelope routing, an optional registration and a non-cascading delete are the foundation

tasks.summary: 113 tasks in 11 phases: setup, three foundational pull requests, one pull request per user story (US3, US1, US2 first), polish and measurement

approach: FBL library first (bullets family, declared registration blocks, drift), then envelope routing with an optional registration, then the module's model with the fixtures, then a shared hierarchy surface (session contract, wire, client library), then one pull request per remaining user story.
